title: AI Stocks Are the Most Hated Trade Right Now. The Numbers Say Otherwise
creator: Couch Investor
summary: Couch Investor argues the AI selloff is a sentiment move, not broken fundamentals. He opens with Peter Lynch clips on having the stomach for drawdowns and not needing near-term money in stocks, then notes the chip index (SOX) is down 26.7% and names like Nebius, Lam Research and Applied Materials are near 50% off their highs, even though the sector keeps beating expectations: TSMC revenue up 41.2% with Q4 guidance up 58%, Nvidia data-centre revenue more than doubled last quarter, and Broadcom AI revenue up 221% with guidance to roughly double twice to $230B. He flags Meta turning free-cash-flow negative on capex, and the roughly $2.3T of contracted demand as a risk if OpenAI and Anthropic cannot fund their commitments, with Oracle the most indebted of the group. Historically the SOX has taken about 54 calendar days to rebound; he also cites Tom Lee calling the selloff near its end. Nebius is his poster-child neocloud, planning 1GW of Vera Rubin capacity in 2027. He makes no explicit ticker call: long-term holders may find opportunities now, but waiting for next week's Fed meeting and earnings is also fine. Captions garble some names (Nebius, Anthropic) and one hedge-fund statistic.
